title: Projective Functors and the Soergel Functor in Category O

items.title: The coinvariant algebra of a finite Weyl group
items.statement: Let $\mathfrak g$ be a finite-dimensional complex semisimple Lie algebra with Cartan subalgebra $\mathfrak h$ and Weyl group $W$ acting on $\mathfrak h$ by reflections, hence on the symmetric algebra $S=S(\mathfrak h)$ by graded algebra automorphisms. Write $S^W_+$ for the ideal of positive-degree invariants and $I:=S\,S^W_+$ for the ideal of $S$ it generates, so that $I$ is the specialization to the Weyl group of the homogeneous ideal of [[def-finite-linear-invariant-and-coinvariant-polynomial-algebras]]. The **coinvariant algebra** is $$C=C(\mathfrak h,W):=S/I.$$ It is a commutative graded $\mathbb C$-algebra with $C_0=\mathbb C$, a canonical surjection $\rho:S\to C$, and an induced action of $W$ by graded algebra automorphisms; $C$ is finite dimensional because $W$ is generated by reflections. The page fixes the degree normalization $\deg\mathfrak h=2$ used throughout the type-A Soergel material, so that the type-A coordinate model is $S=\mathbb k[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ with the place-permuting $S_n$-action and $C=\mathbb k[x_1,\dots,x_n]/(e_1,\dots,e_n)$ for the elementary symmetric polynomials $e_1,\dots,e_n$. Elements of $C$ are written as classes $\rho(f)$; no choice principle is used.
items.strategy: The published definition is quoted for a finite linear group and specialized to the reflection group case; the quotient by the ideal generated by positive-degree invariants is the same construction because $S^W_+$ is the space of invariants of positive degree. Degree normalization is a convention fixed here once for the whole page; the identification with the coordinate model is the standard polynomial-ring model of $S(\mathfrak h)$, with $e_i$ the basic invariants of the place-permuting $S_n$-action on $\mathbb k[x_1,\dots,x_n]$.

items.title: The regular integral block and its antidominant weight
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice, inherited from the published block theory. Work in category $\mathcal O$ of a finite-dimensional complex semisimple Lie algebra $\mathfrak g$ with the conventions of [[def-bgg-category-o]]: Cartan $\mathfrak h$, positive system with simple roots $\alpha_i$, Weyl group $W$, Weyl vector $ho$ and dot action $w\cdot\lambda=w(\lambda+ho)-ho$. Fix a **regular integral** weight $\lambda$, i.e. $\langle\lambda+ho,\alpha^\veeangle
otin\{0\}$ for every root $\alpha$ and $\lambda$ integral in the sense of [[def-integral-weyl-group-of-a-weight]]; then the integral Weyl group of $\lambda$ is all of $W$, and the linkage class $C=W\cdot\lambda$ has exactly $|W|$ elements. Write $\mathcal O_\lambda:=\mathcal O_C$ for the corresponding block of [[thm-central-character-summands-split-into-linkage-blocks]]; it is a highest-weight category whose simple objects $L(w\cdot\lambda)$, standard objects $\Delta(w\cdot\lambda)=M(w\cdot\lambda)$, costandard objects $
abla(w\cdot\lambda)$ and projective covers $P(w\cdot\lambda)$ are indexed by $w\in W$, with $\Delta(w_0\cdot\lambda)=L(w_0\cdot\lambda)$ the unique simple standard object and the published triangularity $[\Delta(w\cdot\lambda):L(w\cdot\lambda)]=1$ and $[\Delta(w\cdot\lambda):L(v\cdot\lambda)]
eq0\Rightarrow v\cdot\lambda\le w\cdot\lambda$ in the dominance order on the dot orbit ([[thm-bgg-reciprocity]], [[cor-projective-standard-labels-lie-above-the-head]]). The **antidominant** weight in the block is $w_0\cdot\lambda$, where $w_0$ is the longest element; $P(w_0\cdot\lambda)$ is the antidominant projective. The Grothendieck group $K_0(\mathcal O_\lambda)$ has the classes of the standards and of the simples as bases, as on [[def-grothendieck-group-and-character-of-category-o]].
items.strategy: The block decomposition, linkage classes and the description of central characters are the published items; integrality identifies the integral Weyl group with $W$ and hence the linkage class with the $|W|$-element dot orbit; regularity of $\lambda$ fixes the nontriviality of the stabilizer data used by the published translation-functor definitions. Indexing of simples and Vermas, the triangularity of the Verma-flag matrix ([[thm-bgg-reciprocity]] with [[cor-projective-standard-labels-lie-above-the-head]], read in the direction $[\Delta(w\cdot\lambda):L(v\cdot\lambda)]\neq0\Rightarrow v\cdot\lambda\le w\cdot\lambda$) and the Grothendieck-group bases are the published facts.

items.title: Projective functors on a regular integral block
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice, inherited from the published block theory. For a finite-dimensional $\mathfrak h$-semisimple $\mathfrak g$-module $E$ and a block $\mathcal O_\lambda$ as in [[def-regular-integral-category-o-block-and-its-antidominant-weight]], let $\operatorname{pr}_\lambda:\mathcal O\to\mathcal O_\lambda$ be the exact block projection of [[def-translation-functor-between-o-blocks]] and let $$F_E:=\operatorname{pr}_\lambda\circ(E\otimes-)\circ\operatorname{incl}_\lambda:\mathcal O_\lambda\longrightarrow\mathcal O_\lambda .$$ By [[prop-tensoring-with-a-finite-dimensional-module-preserves-category-o]] and [[lem-block-projection-preserves-projectives]] the functor $F_E$ is exact, and by [[lem-tensoring-a-projective-with-a-finite-dimensional-module-is-projective]] it sends projectives to projectives. A **projective functor** on $\mathcal O_\lambda$ is an endofunctor of $\mathcal O_\lambda$ isomorphic to a direct summand of some $F_E$; the full additive subcategory of all such functors (with arbitrary natural transformations as morphisms) is written $\mathcal F_\lambda$. It is closed under finite direct sums, composition, direct summands and passage to adjoints: composition corresponds to $F_E F_{E'}\cong F_{E\otimes E'}$, and $F_{E^*}$ is both a left and a right adjoint of $F_E$, by the published biadjunction for tensoring with duals. Every projective functor is exact and preserves projective objects. This is the definition of [BGe] and [Soe90, Section 1.2]; unlike the functors $T_\lambda^\mu$ of [[def-translation-functor-between-o-blocks]], projective functors are not required to come from a single finite-dimensional tensor functor, only from a summand of one.
items.strategy: All closure properties are inherited from the published tensor and block-projection items: exactness and preservation of projective objects, additivity, and the adjunction for $E^*\otimes-$; direct summands of exact functors are exact after splitting, and the idempotent-completion convention for additive categories is [[def-additive-category]]. The composition identity is the associativity of the tensor product of finite-dimensional modules. No choice is used beyond the inherited AC of the block theory.

items.title: The coinvariant algebra is a complete intersection with one-dimensional socle
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice, inherited from the published invariant-theory items. Let $w_1,\dots,w_r$ be homogeneous basic invariants of the finite Weyl group $W$ acting on $\mathfrak h$, of page degrees $2d_1,\dots,2d_r$ so that $d_1,\dots,d_r$ are the classical basic degrees (the degrees with $\deg\mathfrak h=1$; in the type-A model $d_1,\dots,d_r=1,\dots,n$), $S(\mathfrak h)^W=\mathbb C[w_1,\dots,w_r]$, and $\rho$ is the quotient by the ideal $I=(w_1,\dots,w_r)$. Put $N:=\sum_{i=1}^r(d_i-1)$; the top degree of the coinvariant algebra $C$ of [[def-the-coinvariant-algebra-of-a-finite-weyl-group]] is then $2N$. Then: (1) $w_1,\dots,w_r$ is a homogeneous regular sequence in $S$ and $C$ is a complete intersection: $C=S/(w_1,\dots,w_r)$ with $\operatorname{Hilb}(C,t)=\prod_i(1-t^{2d_i})/(1-t^2)^r$, $\dim C_{2N}=1$, $C_j=0$ for $j>2N$; (2) the multiplication pairing $C_i\times C_{2N-i}\to C_{2N}\cong\mathbb C$ is nondegenerate for every $i$, and consequently the socle $\operatorname{soc}(C)=\{c\in C: C_+c=0\}$ equals $C_{2N}$ and is one dimensional; (3) equivalently, $C$ is a graded Gorenstein algebra whose socle sits in the top degree $2N$.
items.strategy: By [[lem-reflection-basic-invariants-form-a-regular-sequence]] the basic invariants form a homogeneous regular sequence and [[cor-koszul-complex-resolves-a-regular-quotient]] gives that the Koszul complex $K(w_1,\dots,w_r)$ is a finite free $S$-resolution of $C$; the Hilbert series of (1) is the standard Koszul-complex computation and is also the published [[lem-weyl-coinvariant-hilbert-series-has-order-w-dimension]]. The Koszul complex of a homogeneous regular sequence is self-dual up to the twist $2N=2\sum(d_i-1)$ (its dual is again a Koszul complex on the same sequence), which identifies $\operatorname{Ext}^r_S(C,S)$ with $C(-2N)$ and shows $C$ is Gorenstein of socle degree $2N$; equivalently, one reads off $\dim C_{2N-i}=\dim C_i$ from the symmetry $\operatorname{Hilb}(C,t)=t^{2N}\operatorname{Hilb}(C,t^{-1})$ of the displayed series and then shows that no element of degree $<2N$ is killed by $C_+$: for a nonzero class $c\in C_i$, $i<2N$, there is $c'\in C_{2N-i}$ with $cc'\neq0$, because the top-degree component of $C$ is one dimensional and generated by products of elements of complementary degrees.

items.title: The harmonic complement of the coinvariant algebra
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice, inherited from the published invariant-theory items. Let $W$ act on $\mathfrak h$ by reflections and on $S=S(\mathfrak h)$ by graded algebra automorphisms, with coinvariant algebra $C=S/I$ as in [[def-the-coinvariant-algebra-of-a-finite-weyl-group]]. Then there is a $W$-stable graded subspace $\mathcal H\subseteq S$ such that the multiplication map $$S^W\otimes_{\mathbb C}\mathcal H\longrightarrow S,\qquad p\otimes h\mapsto ph,$$ is an isomorphism of graded $S^W$-modules and $W$-modules, and the restriction of the quotient map $\rho:S\to C$ to $\mathcal H$ is an isomorphism of graded $W$-modules $\mathcal H\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }C$. One may take $\mathcal H=\{f\in S:\partial_p f=0\text{ for all }p\in S^W_+\}$ for the $W$-equivariant Laplacian attached to a $W$-invariant positive definite form on $\mathfrak h_{\mathbb R}$, or any $W$-stable graded complement of $I$; in particular $\dim\mathcal H_d=\dim C_d$ for all $d$, $\dim\mathcal H=|W|$ and $\mathcal H$ is the sum of all $W$-submodules of $S$ not meeting $S^W_+S$.
items.strategy: Choose a positive definite $W$-invariant real form on $\mathfrak h$ (the Killing form restricts to one, and finiteness of $W$ allows averaging); extend it to a positive definite Hermitian form on each finite-dimensional graded piece $S_d$ for which the adjoint of multiplication is differentiation. Because $I$ and $S^W_+$ are $W$-stable and the form is $W$-invariant, the orthogonal complement $\mathcal H_d:=I_d^{\perp}$ is $W$-stable and $S_d=I_d\oplus\mathcal H_d$; hence $\mathcal H$ is a graded $W$-submodule and the restriction of $\rho$ is injective with image spanned by $\mathcal H$, giving $\mathcal H\cong C$ as graded $W$-modules. The isomorphism $S^W\otimes\mathcal H\to S$ follows by comparing graded ranks: $S$ is free of rank $|W|$ over $S^W$ by [[thm-chevalley-shephard-todd-for-finite-weyl-groups]], the map is $S^W$-linear and graded, and modulo $S^W_+$ it reduces to the isomorphism $\mathcal H\to C$ induced by $\rho$; graded Nakayama over the graded-local ring $S^W$ makes it surjective, and the rank count (both sides are free of rank $|W|$ over $S^W$) makes it injective. This is the reflection-group case of the harmonic-complement argument used on the published $S(\mathfrak g)$-page; only finite-dimensional linear algebra and the published freeness are used.

items.title: The wall-crossing functor and its unit and counit
items.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice, inherited from the published translation-functor items. Let $(\lambda,\mu,\alpha)$ be a single-wall translation datum of [[def-dot-action-facets-and-single-wall-translation-data]] with regular integral $\lambda$, wall reflection $s=s_\alpha$ and translating weight $
u$, and let $T_\lambda^\mu:\mathcal O_\lambda	o\mathcal O_\mu$ and $T_\mu^\lambda:\mathcal O_\mu	o\mathcal O_\lambda$ be the translation functors of [[def-translation-functor-between-o-blocks]]. The **wall-crossing functor** attached to $s$ is $$	heta_s:=T^\lambda_\mu\circ T^\mu_\lambda\colon\mathcal O_\lambda\longrightarrow\mathcal O_\lambda .$$ It is a projective functor in the sense of [[def-projective-functors-on-a-regular-integral-category-o-block]]: it is a direct summand of $F_{L(
u)\otimes L(
u)^*}$ for the translating simple $L(
u)$. The biadjunction of [[prop-translation-functors-are-exact-and-biadjoint-across-a-wall]] gives natural transformations $\eta:\operatorname{id}	o	heta_s$ (unit, from the adjunction $T^\mu_\lambda\dashv T^\lambda_\mu$) and $\varepsilon:	heta_s	o\operatorname{id}$ (counit, from the biadjunction in the other direction) satisfying the triangle identities; both are declared part of the data. Up to natural equivalence $	heta_s$ depends only on the wall of $s$ and the chosen block, not on $\mu$ or on the chosen translating weight.
items.strategy: The composite of two exact functors preserving projectives is a projective functor, and the identification of $\theta_s$ with a summand of $F_{L(\nu)\otimes L(\nu)^*}$ is the decomposition of the tensor square of the translating simple; the biadjunction maps are the explicit unit and counit obtained from the two adjunction identities of the published proposition. Independence of $\mu$ is the standard wall-crossing independence: two wall weights differ by an integral weight in the wall and the corresponding translation functors are naturally isomorphic on the block, as displayed in the published theorem's conventions.

items.title: Wall-crossing acts on standard modules by a two-step extension
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice, inherited from the published items. Let $\theta_s$ be the wall-crossing functor of [[def-wall-crossing-functor-and-unit-counit]] attached to the simple reflection $s$ in the regular integral block $\mathcal O_\lambda$. For every $w\in W$ the object $\theta_s\Delta(w\cdot\lambda)$ has a finite Verma flag with exactly two factors, namely $\Delta(w\cdot\lambda)$ and $\Delta(ws\cdot\lambda)$, each with multiplicity one; in the Grothendieck group $$[\theta_s\Delta(w\cdot\lambda)]=[\Delta(w\cdot\lambda)]+[\Delta(ws\cdot\lambda)].$$ Moreover the functor is exact and preserves Verma-filtered objects and finite Verma flags: if $X$ has a finite Verma flag with multiplicities $(X:\Delta(v\cdot\lambda))$, then $\theta_s X$ has one with multiplicity $(\theta_s X:\Delta(u\cdot\lambda))=(X:\Delta(u\cdot\lambda))+(X:\Delta(us\cdot\lambda))$, and the same formula holds for the images in the Grothendieck group. This is the wall-crossing computation of [Soe90, Section 2.1] in the form supplied by the published wall-translation theorem; the resulting flag is not in general split, but splitting is not asserted or used here.
items.strategy: Apply [[thm-translation-to-and-from-a-wall-on-standard-modules]]: $T_\mu^\lambda\Delta(w\cdot\mu)\cong\Delta(w\cdot\lambda)$ after translating to the wall, and the return translation has a two-factor flag with factors $\Delta(w\cdot\lambda)$ and $\Delta(ws\cdot\lambda)$, each of multiplicity one, ordered by the Bruhat order of the wall stabilizer. Composing these two statements gives the flag of $\theta_s\Delta(w\cdot\lambda)$. Exactness of $\theta_s$ (as a projective functor) and additivity over finite flags, together with the independence of the flag [[lem-verma-flag-multiplicities-are-independent-of-the-flag]], upgrade the single-factor computation to the stated flag formula for arbitrary Verma-filtered $X$; subquotients of filtered objects are handled by [[lem-direct-summands-of-verma-filtered-objects-are-verma-filtered]].

items.title: The coinvariant algebra is the graded regular representation of W
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice, inherited from the published invariant-theory items. Let $W$ be a finite Weyl group with reflection representation $\mathfrak h$, coinvariant algebra $C=S(\mathfrak h)/S(\mathfrak h)S^W_+$ and basic degrees $d_1,\dots,d_r$ as in [[def-the-coinvariant-algebra-of-a-finite-weyl-group]]. Then: (1) $C\cong\mathbb C W$ as a $W$-module: $C$ is isomorphic to the regular representation of $W$; (2) the graded $W$-character of $C$ is $$\operatorname{HTr}(C,t)(w):=\sum_{i\ge0}t^{i}\operatorname{tr}(w\mid C_i)=\prod_{i=1}^r(1-t^{2d_i})\cdot\det(1-t^2w\mid\mathfrak h^*)^{-1}\qquad(w\in W),$$ where $d_1,\dots,d_r$ are the classical basic degrees of [[lem-the-coinvariant-algebra-is-a-gorenstein-algebra-with-one-dimensional-socle]], an identity of rational functions whose value at $t=1$ is $|W|$ for $w=1$ and $0$ for $w\neq1$; (3) equivalently, $C$ is the graded lift of the regular representation: writing $\operatorname{mult}_E(C,t)$ for the graded multiplicity of the irreducible $W$-module $E$, the identity $\sum_E\operatorname{mult}_E(C,t)\,\chi_E(w)=\operatorname{HTr}(C,t)(w)$ determines the graded multiplicities uniquely, with $\operatorname{mult}_E(C,1)=\dim E$ the multiplicity of $E$ in the regular representation. The Hilbert-series specialization of (2) at $w=1$ is $\prod_i(1+t^2+\dots+t^{2(d_i-1)})$, the published formula in the page's $\deg\mathfrak h=2$ normalization.
items.strategy: By [[lem-the-harmonic-complement-of-the-coinvariant-algebra]] the quotient map restricts to an isomorphism $\mathcal H\cong C$ of graded $W$-modules with $S=S^W\otimes\mathcal H$, so $\operatorname{HTr}(C,t)=\operatorname{HTr}(\mathcal H,t)$ and, since $S^W$ contributes the scalar factor $\prod_i(1-t^{d_i})^{-1}$ to the graded trace of $S$, the identities of the published Hilbert-series lemma give $\operatorname{HTr}(C,t)=\operatorname{HTr}(S,t)\cdot\prod_i(1-t^{2d_i})$ with $\operatorname{HTr}(S,t)(w)=\det(1-t^2w|\mathfrak h^*)^{-1}$ (Molien's formula, proved there). For (1): evaluate at $t\to1$. The numerator vanishes to order exactly $r$ and the denominator to order $\dim\mathfrak h^w$; for $w\neq1$ the reflection representation is faithful, so $\dim\mathfrak h^w\le\dim\mathfrak h-1=r-1$ and the numerator order exceeds the denominator order, giving limit $0$ for $w\neq1$; at $w=1$ the limit is $\prod_i d_i=|W|$ by the published dimension formula. A finite-dimensional $\mathbb C$-representation is determined up to isomorphism by its character, so $C\cong\mathbb C W$ as $W$-modules. Part (3) is the standard description of graded $W$-modules by their graded characters and Krull-Schmidt uniqueness for the semisimple category of finite-dimensional $W$-modules over $\mathbb C$. The computation is choice-free except for the inherited AC of the published Hilbert-series lemma.

items.title: The wall-crossing action on the Grothendieck group is multiplication by 1+s
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice, inherited from the published items. In the regular integral block $\mathcal O_\lambda$ of [[def-regular-integral-category-o-block-and-its-antidominant-weight]] the assignment $$c\colon K_0(\mathcal O_\lambda)\longrightarrow\mathbb Z[W],\qquad [\Delta(w\cdot\lambda)]\longmapsto w,$$ is an isomorphism of abelian groups, and for every simple reflection $s$ the wall-crossing functor $\theta_s$ of [[def-wall-crossing-functor-and-unit-counit]] satisfies $$c\,[\theta_s X]=c\,[X]\cdot(1+s)\qquad\text{for all }X\in\mathcal O_\lambda,$$ i.e. right multiplication by $1+s$ in the integral group ring $\mathbb Z[W]$. Consequently $c$ intertwines the wall-crossing action with the right regular action of $\mathbb Z[W]$ generated by the elements $1+s$; in particular the classes $[\theta_{s_1}\cdots\theta_{s_k}M(\lambda)]$ for a reduced expression $w=s_1\cdots s_k$ satisfy $c[\theta_{s_1}\cdots\theta_{s_k}M(\lambda)]=w$.
items.strategy: The class of any object is the sum of the classes of the factors of a finite Verma flag, and [[prop-the-grothendieck-group-of-o-has-simple-and-standard-bases]] gives that the Verma classes form a basis; since the block has $|W|$ Verma classes indexed by $W$, the assignment is an isomorphism of free abelian groups. The formula $[\theta_s\Delta(w\cdot\lambda)]=[\Delta(w\cdot\lambda)]+[\Delta(ws\cdot\lambda)]$ of [[lem-wall-crossing-functors-act-on-standard-modules-by-the-two-step-extension]], applied factor by factor using exactness of $\theta_s$, gives $c[\theta_s X]=c[X]\cdot(1+s)$ on the Verma basis, hence on the whole group; the right multiplication by $s$ acts by $w\mapsto ws$ on the basis, giving the displayed convention. The final sentence is the iteration of the formula over a reduced expression.

items.title: Wall-crossing compositions produce the projective with the top standard label
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice, inherited from the published items. Fix a reduced expression $w=s_1s_2\cdots s_k$ in $W$ and let $\theta_w:=\theta_{s_1}\theta_{s_2}\cdots\theta_{s_k}$. Then the projective object $\theta_w\Delta(\lambda)$ of the regular integral block satisfies $$\theta_w\Delta(\lambda)\ \cong\ P(w\cdot\lambda)\ \oplus\ \bigoplus_{x<w}P(x\cdot\lambda)^{\oplus m_x},\qquad m_x\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0},$$ and the multiplicities $m_x$ are determined by the class $c[\theta_w\Delta(\lambda)]=w$ of [[lem-wall-crossing-functors-act-on-the-grothendieck-group-by-right-multiplication-by-one-plus-s]] together with the unitriangularity $(P(x\cdot\lambda):\Delta(y\cdot\lambda))=[\Delta(y\cdot\lambda):L(x\cdot\lambda)]$ of BGG reciprocity; in particular $P(w\cdot\lambda)$ is the unique indecomposable direct summand of $\theta_w\Delta(\lambda)$ whose Verma flag contains $\Delta(w\cdot\lambda)$, and it appears there with multiplicity one. Consequently every indecomposable projective of the block is a direct summand of some $\theta_w\Delta(\lambda)$, $w\in W$.
items.strategy: $\theta_w\Delta(\lambda)$ is projective, being obtained from $\Delta(\lambda)$ by projective functors, so it is a finite direct sum of indecomposable projectives $P(x\cdot\lambda)$ with multiplicities determined by their heads. The Verma-flag multiplicity $(P(x\cdot\lambda):\Delta(y\cdot\lambda))$ is computed by [[thm-bgg-reciprocity]]; [[cor-projective-standard-labels-lie-above-the-head]] gives $(P(x\cdot\lambda):\Delta(y\cdot\lambda))\neq0\Rightarrow y\ge x$ and $(P(x\cdot\lambda):\Delta(x\cdot\lambda))=1$, so the matrix is unitriangular and the multiplicities $m_x$ are read off from the known class $\sum_{y\le w}[\Delta(y\cdot\lambda)]$ by descending induction on the Bruhat order. The summand with label $w$ occurs with multiplicity one by unitriangularity, and the last sentence iterates over $w\in W$ using that the classes $w$ generate $\mathbb Z[W]$.

items.title: Indecomposable projective functors are indexed by the Weyl group
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice, inherited from the published items. On the regular integral block $\mathcal O_\lambda$: (1) every projective functor is a finite direct sum of indecomposable projective functors (the category $\mathcal F_\lambda$ is Krull-Schmidt); (2) the indecomposable projective functors are indexed by the elements of $W$; the functor $\Theta_w$ corresponding to $w$ is characterized by the properties that it is a direct summand of every composite $\theta_{s_1}\cdots\theta_{s_k}$ with $s_1\cdots s_k$ a reduced expression for $w$, appearing there with multiplicity one and with all other indecomposable summands indexed by $x<w$ in the Bruhat order, and that $\Theta_w(\Delta(v\cdot\lambda))$ has no direct summand with Verma head labelled $y$ unless $y\ge w$. In particular the indecomposable projective functors of the block are generated by the wall-crossing functors: every one of them is a direct summand of a composition $\theta_{s_1}\cdots\theta_{s_k}$. (3) Two projective functors are naturally equivalent if and only if their induced operators on $K_0(\mathcal O_\lambda)$ agree.
items.strategy: This is the classification of [BGe] specialized to the regular integral block. The route: (i) functors $F_E$ preserve the locally finite central-character subcategories, and a projective functor is determined by its restriction to the block (its direct summands correspond to direct summands of a single module, [BGe, Section 0.2]); (ii) for projective functors $F,G$ the canonical map $\operatorname{Hom}(F,G)\to\operatorname{Hom}(FM_\lambda,GM_\lambda)$ is injective, and bijective for dominant $\lambda$ [BGe, Theorem 3.5], proved by the completion argument in [BGe, Section 3.6]; (iii) the corollary [BGe, Section 3.8] continues an isomorphism or decomposition of $FM_\lambda\cong GM_\lambda$ to the functors, giving (1) and reducing (2) to the classification of indecomposable projectives in the target block, where [BGe, Theorem 3.3(ii)] identifies the functor $F_\xi$ by $F_\xi(M_\chi)=P_\psi$ for $\xi=(\psi,\chi)$ written properly; (iv) the block's indecomposable projectives are indexed by $W$ (published enough-projectives and projective-cover theory), and the summands of the $\theta_w$ realize all of them by [[lem-wall-crossing-compositions-produce-the-projective-with-the-top-standard-label]]; (v) determination on the Grothendieck group is [BGe, Theorem 3.4(i)] with the identification of the class operators via [[lem-wall-crossing-functors-act-on-the-grothendieck-group-by-right-multiplication-by-one-plus-s]] and the published reachability of every simple by finite-dimensional tensoring.

items.title: The deformed category O family over the Cartan symmetric algebra
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $S=S(\mathfrak h)$ be the symmetric algebra of the Cartan subalgebra, graded by $\deg\mathfrak h=2$, and let $\mathfrak b=\mathfrak h\oplus\mathfrak n^+$ act on $S\otimes\mathbb C_\lambda$ by $x\cdot(s\otimes1)=xs\otimes1+\lambda(x)s\otimes1$ for $x\in\mathfrak h$ and $x\cdot(s\otimes1)=xs\otimes1$ for $x\in\mathfrak n^+$, where $xs$ denotes the action of $\mathfrak b\to\mathfrak h$ on $S$ by weight. Put $M_S(\lambda):=U(\mathfrak g)\otimes_{\mathfrak b}(S\otimes\mathbb C_\lambda)\in \mathfrak g\otimes S$-mod, with the right $S$-module structure by multiplication on the last factor, so that $M_S(\lambda)\otimes_S\mathbb C_\epsilon\cong M(\lambda+\epsilon)$ for every $\epsilon\in\mathfrak h^*$. For a localization $T$ of $S$ put $M_T(\lambda):=M_S(\lambda)\otimes_S T$ and let $\mathcal D_T(\lambda)$ be the full subcategory of $\mathfrak g\otimes T$-modules that are direct summands of a finite direct sum of modules $E\otimes M_T(\lambda)$ for finite-dimensional $\mathfrak g$-modules $E$; write $\mathcal D_R(\lambda)$ for the localization $R=S_{(0)}$ at the origin of $\operatorname{Spec} S$. The **deformed family** is the assignment $T\mapsto\mathcal D_T(\lambda)$ together with the specialization functors $-\otimes_T\mathbb C_\epsilon$ at the closed points $\epsilon$ of $\operatorname{Spec} T$; for $\epsilon$ in a Zariski-open set the specialization lies in the regular integral block $\mathcal O_{\lambda+\epsilon}$. Modules in $\mathcal D_T(\lambda)$ carry an $\mathfrak h$-weight decomposition with locally free finite-rank weight spaces. The conventions are those of [Soe90, Section 2.1].
items.strategy: The construction is the standard universal family of Verma modules with a formal deformation parameter; the twisted $\mathfrak b$-action makes the fiber at $\epsilon$ the Verma module of weight $\lambda+\epsilon$, the right $S$-action commutes with $\mathfrak g$, and direct summands of finite tensor products give the analogue of the projective functors of [[def-projective-functors-on-a-regular-integral-category-o-block]] over $T$. Weight spaces are locally free by the PBW model of Verma modules; no choice beyond the inherited AC of the block theory is used.

items.title: Base change, freeness and specialization in the deformed family
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. In the deformed family of [[def-the-deformed-category-o-family-and-its-specializations]] with $T$ a localization of $S=S(\mathfrak h)$ and $M,N\in\mathcal D_T(\lambda)$: (1) the canonical map $$U(\mathfrak g)\otimes_Z T\longrightarrow \big(\operatorname{End}_T(M_T(\lambda))\big)^{\mathfrak g\text{-finite}},\qquad u\otimes t\longmapsto\big(m\mapsto u\cdot m\cdot t\big),$$ is an isomorphism of $T$-algebras, the superscript denoting the $\mathfrak g$-finite part for the adjoint action $X\cdot f=X\circ f-f\circ X$, and $Z=Z(U(\mathfrak g))$ acting on $T$ through the Harish-Chandra isomorphism followed by the shift $+\lambda$; (2) $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g\otimes T}(E\otimes M_T(\lambda),F\otimes M_T(\lambda))$ is a free $T$-module of rank $\dim(E\otimes F^*)_0$ for finite-dimensional $E,F$, where the subscript denotes the zero weight space, and the natural base-change map $$\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g\otimes T}(M,N)\otimes_T\mathbb C_\epsilon\longrightarrow \operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g\otimes\mathbb C}(M\otimes_T\mathbb C_\epsilon,N\otimes_T\mathbb C_\epsilon)$$ is an isomorphism for every $\epsilon\in\operatorname{Spec} T$; (3) $\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathfrak g\otimes T}(M,N)$ is locally free of finite rank over $T$; (4) if a $T$-linear map of objects of $\mathcal D_R(\lambda)$ is an isomorphism on the special fiber at $0$, it is an isomorphism (Nakayama).
items.strategy: The route is [Soe90, Section 2.1]: (1) is the structure theorem for the relative enveloping algebra acting on the universal family, attributed there to [So1] and used to identify the $\mathfrak g\otimes S$-endomorphisms of the family; (2) part (a) follows from (1) and the classical description of $U(\mathfrak g)$ as a $Z$-module via Kostant harmonics, and part (b) is the base-change computation using Jantzen, Einhullende Algebren halbeinfacher Lie-Algebren, 7.25, plus the elementary lemma on $\operatorname{Hom}_R(R/I,N)$ for finitely generated $I$ and flat extensions; (3) is [Soe90, Proposition 3(a)] with the weight-space decomposition of Lemma 1; (4) is Proposition 4, proved by Nakayama's lemma over the local ring. Step (1) is the structure theorem for the universal family [So1, Section 1.2 and Corollary 8 in Section 3.5]: for a Borel subgroup the relative enveloping algebra coincides with $U(\mathfrak g)\otimes_Z S$, and Corollary 8 identifies its $\mathfrak g$-finite endomorphisms with $U(\mathfrak g)\otimes_Z S$. Step (b) is the base-change input [Ja, 7.25]; the library records it here as an input, not as a proved local supplier.

items.title: Lifting of indecomposable projectives to the deformed family
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. In the notation of [[def-the-deformed-category-o-family-and-its-specializations]] let $\lambda\in\mathfrak h^*$ be dominant and regular, let $A$ be its $\mathbb Z$-coset in $\mathfrak h^*/P$, let $W_A$ be the corresponding Weyl group and let $R$ be the local ring of $S$ at $0$. Then for every $z\in W_A$ there is an object $P_R(z,\lambda)\in\mathcal D_R(\lambda)$, well defined up to isomorphism, with $P_R(z,\lambda)\otimes_R\mathbb C\cong P(z\cdot\lambda)$, and every indecomposable object of $\mathcal D_R(\lambda)$ is isomorphic to one of the $P_R(z,\lambda)$; the objects are obtained inductively by applying a single finite-dimensional tensor functor to $M_R(\lambda)$ and passing to the component whose special fiber is the summand with largest Bruhat label, which is split off by lifting a splitting along the open set of [[prop-base-change-freeness-and-specialization-in-the-deformed-family]]; the same statement holds for singular dominant $\lambda$ with $W_A$ replaced by the stabilizer $W_{A,\lambda}$.
items.strategy: [Soe90, Theorem 6]: induction on $\ell(z)$. For $z=e$ take $P_R(\lambda)=M_R(\lambda)$. For general $z$, let $E$ be the simple finite-dimensional module with extremal weight $z\cdot\lambda-\lambda$; in $E\otimes M_R(\lambda)$ the label $z$ occurs exactly once and is maximal for the Bruhat order on the special fiber, so after localizing to a smaller affine open set the splitting inclusion of the sum of the lifted projectives $\bigoplus_{y\neq z}P_R(y,\lambda)$ extends to a split inclusion into the relevant component by [[prop-base-change-freeness-and-specialization-in-the-deformed-family]] (Propositions 3 and 4 there); the cokernel is the desired $P_R(z,\lambda)$. Well-definedness up to isomorphism is Nakayama's lemma over the local ring; the description of all indecomposables follows since every indecomposable of $\mathcal D_R(\lambda)$ is a summand of an $E\otimes M_R(\lambda)$.

items.title: The central action on the deformed antidominant projective
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\lambda$ be dominant and regular, $R$ the local ring of $S$ at $0$, $P_R:=P_R(w_0,\lambda)$ the deformed antidominant projective of [[thm-lifting-of-indecomposable-projectives-to-the-deformed-family]], and let $\Phi\colon Z(U(\mathfrak g))\to T$ be the Harish-Chandra map followed by the shift $+\lambda$ and the structure map to $T$. Then: (1) the kernel of $\Phi$ annihilates $P_R(w_0,\lambda)$: an element $z$ of the center acts on $P_R$ by the scalar $\Phi(z)$ determined by its action on a generic Verma constituent; (2) the multiplication $Z\to\operatorname{End}_{\mathfrak g\otimes T}P_R$ is surjective with kernel $\ker\Phi$, and it induces a canonical isomorphism $$\operatorname{End}_{\mathfrak g\otimes T}P_R(w_0,\lambda)\ \cong\ T\otimes_{T^{W}}T,$$ compatible with the central maps $Z\to T\otimes_{T^{W}}T$, $z\mapsto\Phi(z)\otimes1$, and specializing at the closed fiber to the Endomorphismensatz $\operatorname{End}_{\mathfrak g}P(w_0\cdot\lambda)\cong C$; (3) under wall-crossing the central actions are intertwined: for dominant $\lambda,\mu$ with $\mu$ regular and $\lambda$ in the wall closure, the diagram of maps $Z\to\operatorname{End}$ commutes with the natural identification of the two deformed antidominant projectives.
items.strategy: [Soe90, Lemmas 3 and 4 and Theorem 8, preprint pp. 11-14]. (1): spread the deformed projective out to an affine open set $T$ (Proposition 5), use the Verma flag of the specializations (Lemma 1) and compare the actions of $z$ and of $j\circ\tilde\Phi(z)\in T$ on each Verma constituent by the generic-series computation; Proposition 3's freeness plus passing to the special fiber gives the statement. (2): surjectivity of the two maps follows by the same generic-versus-special fiber comparison together with the dimension count $\dim C=|W|$; the image is the invariant part of the shifted Harish-Chandra map, and the kernels agree by (1). (3): [Soe90, Theorem 8], proved by reducing to the completed local ring and comparing the two actions on $\bigoplus_n M_R(\lambda)\otimes_R R/\mathfrak m^n$; the commutation on each finite quotient follows from the equality of the two induced maps $Z\to R/\mathfrak m^n$.

items.title: The endomorphisms of the antidominant projective form the coinvariant algebra
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\mathfrak g$ be finite-dimensional complex semisimple, $\lambda$ a regular integral weight and $\mathcal O_\lambda$ its block with antidominant weight $w_0\cdot\lambda$. Let $C$ be the coinvariant algebra of [[def-the-coinvariant-algebra-of-a-finite-weyl-group]] for the Cartan reflection representation, with its grading fixed there. Then: (1) the natural maps $Z(U(\mathfrak g))\to C$ (Harish-Chandra isomorphism, shifted by $\lambda$, followed by the quotient map $\rho$) and $Z(U(\mathfrak g))\to\operatorname{End}_{\mathfrak g}P(w_0\cdot\lambda)$ (multiplication) are surjective with the same kernel; (2) consequently the multiplication map induces a canonical algebra isomorphism $$\operatorname{End}_{\mathfrak g}P(w_0\cdot\lambda)\ \cong\ C,$$ identifying $C$ with the endomorphism ring of the antidominant projective, canonically and independently of the choice of projective cover inside its isomorphism class; (3) the grading on the right-hand side is the internal grading of the coinvariant algebra; no graded lift of category $\mathcal O$ is asserted or used. This is Soergel's Endomorphismensatz [Soe90, Theorem 7], in the regular integral case; the companion general form for singular blocks replaces $C$ by the invariants $C^{W_\lambda}$.
items.strategy: [Soe90, Section 2.2]. Surjectivity with common kernel of the two maps is [[lem-the-central-action-on-the-deformed-antidominant-projective]](2), applied to the deformation of $P(w_0\cdot\lambda)$; specialization at $\epsilon=0$ identifies the deformed antidominant projective with $P(w_0\cdot\lambda)$ by [[thm-lifting-of-indecomposable-projectives-to-the-deformed-family]]. The identification of the target of the first map with $C$ uses [[lem-weyl-orbit-sums-form-a-basis-of-finite-weyl-invariants]] (the image is the full invariant ring, and for regular $\lambda$ the relevant stabilizer is trivial); the dimensions agree by [[lem-the-coinvariant-algebra-is-a-gorenstein-algebra-with-one-dimensional-socle]] ($\dim C=|W|$) and the deformed dimension count. Since the two maps have the same kernel and the same target, the factorization through $\operatorname{End}P(w_0\cdot\lambda)$ is an isomorphism.

items.title: The antidominant projective and the Soergel functor
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice, inherited from the published items. In the regular integral block $\mathcal O_\lambda$ of [[def-regular-integral-category-o-block-and-its-antidominant-weight]] fix the antidominant weight $w_0\cdot\lambda$ and let $P:=P(w_0\cdot\lambda)$ be a projective cover of $L(w_0\cdot\lambda)$; it is unique up to isomorphism and indecomposable by [[prop-projective-covers-in-o-are-indecomposable-and-unique]], and it is an injective object of $\mathcal O_\lambda$. The **Soergel functor** is $$V:=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O}(P,-)\colon\mathcal O_\lambda\longrightarrow \operatorname{End}_{\mathcal O}(P)^{\mathrm{op}}\text{-mod},\qquad M\longmapsto \operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O}(P,M),$$ with the action of $\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal O}(P)$ induced by composition of endomorphisms of $P$. Its values on the standard objects and on the indecomposable projectives are written $V\Delta(w\cdot\lambda):=V(\Delta(w\cdot\lambda))$ and $VP(w\cdot\lambda):=V(P(w\cdot\lambda))$; the choice of projective cover changes $V$ by a natural equivalence only. The functor is left exact, and $VP\cong\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal O}(P)$ with the regular module structure.
items.strategy: The definition packages the published projective-cover theory of the block; the injectivity of $P$ in the block is the standard self-duality statement for the antidominant projective (it follows from the published existence of enough projectives and the block's highest-weight duality). Left exactness of $\operatorname{Hom}(P,-)$ is formal. No choice beyond the inherited AC is used.

items.title: Soergel's Struktursatz: the functor V is fully faithful on projectives
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\mathcal O_\lambda$ be a regular integral block with antidominant projective $P=P(w_0\cdot\lambda)$ and Soergel functor $V=\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O}(P,-)$, and let $C$ be the coinvariant algebra, identified with $\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal O}(P)$ by [[thm-endomorphisms-of-the-antidominant-projective-are-the-coinvariant-algebra]], so that $V$ takes values in $C$-modules. Then for every $M\in\mathcal O_\lambda$ and every projective $Q\in\mathcal O_\lambda$ the canonical map $$V\colon \operatorname{Hom}_{\mathcal O_\lambda}(M,Q)\longrightarrow \operatorname{Hom}_{C\text{-mod}}(VM,VQ)$$ is an isomorphism. In particular $V$ is fully faithful on the full subcategory of projective objects of the block, and it is faithful on all of $\mathcal O_\lambda$ after passing to the quotient by the Serre subcategory of objects killed by $V$.
items.strategy: [Soe90, Section 2.3, Struktursatz 9]. Step 1 (injectivity): if $\phi\colon M\to Q$ is nonzero, its image has a nonzero Bruhat-maximal Verma constituent, and the corresponding composition with $P\to M(w_0\cdot\lambda)$ gives $V\phi\neq0$; this uses that $Q$ has a finite Verma flag and the Socle Lemma 6 ($M(\lambda)=\{v\in P: C_+v=0\}$, proved from the one-dimensional socle of $C$ of [[lem-the-coinvariant-algebra-is-a-gorenstein-algebra-with-one-dimensional-socle]]). Step 2: the statement is true for $Q=P$ because $P$ and $C$ are injective objects of the respective categories and the claim reduces to simple $M$ and the five lemma; then for $Q=\Delta(\lambda)$ one takes the $C_+$-torsion subspaces of the isomorphism for $Q=P$ (Lemma 6). Step 3 (general projective $Q$): every projective of the block is a direct summand of $F(M(\lambda))$ for a projective functor $F$ of [[def-projective-functors-on-a-regular-integral-category-o-block]], and for $Q=F(M(\lambda))$ the claim follows from the adjunction $G\dashv F$ with $VG\cong GV$ on the $C$-module side: $\operatorname{Hom}(M,FM(\lambda))=\operatorname{Hom}(GM,M(\lambda))=\operatorname{Hom}_C(VGM,VM(\lambda))=\operatorname{Hom}_C(VM,VFM(\lambda))$, the middle isomorphism being Step 2. The quotient-category adjunction that makes $F$ descend to $C$-modules is [Soe90, Lemma 5], a general lemma on adjoint pairs of exact functors and dense subcategories. The identification of the projective summands of $F(M(\lambda))$ with the indecomposables follows from [[thm-indecomposable-projective-functors-are-indexed-by-the-weyl-group]] and [[prop-projective-covers-in-o-are-indecomposable-and-unique]], and the reachability of each block's simples by finite-dimensional tensoring is [[lem-finite-dimensional-tensors-reach-every-block-simple]].

items.title: Wall-crossing under the Soergel functor is tensoring with the coinvariant bimodule
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\theta_s$ be the wall-crossing functor on the regular integral block $\mathcal O_\lambda$, let $C$ be the coinvariant algebra identified with $\operatorname{End}(P)$ and let $C^s\subseteq C$ be the invariants of the simple reflection $s$. Then there is a natural isomorphism of functors $\mathcal O_\lambda\to C$-mod $$V\theta_s\ \cong\ \big(C\otimes_{C^s}C\big)\otimes_C V,$$ where $C\otimes_{C^s}C$ is regarded as a left $C$-module via its second factor. More precisely: after choosing the auxiliary grading, the graded form of the identification is $V\theta_s\cong(-\otimes_R B_s)\circ V$ with the polynomial Soergel bimodule $B_s=S\otimes_{S^s}S(1)$, whose standard generators have degrees $\mp1$ ([[def-type-a-soergel-bimodule-for-a-simple-reflection]]); the ungraded isomorphism above is its forgetful image, and the right-coinvariant specialization identifies the rank-one case with $C\otimes_{C^s}C$, generated in degrees $0$ and $2$. The auxiliary suspension between the generators in degrees $\mp1$ and this normalization is fixed by the rank-one case and is not intrinsic to category $\mathcal O$. The resulting dictionary identifies the wall-crossing action on the projective side with tensoring with the reduced Soergel bimodule of the simple reflection.
items.strategy: [Soe90, Section 2.4, Theorem 10 and Corollary 1]: choose the deformed projectives $P_R(w_0,\lambda)$ and $P_R(w_0,\mu)$; by [[lem-the-central-action-on-the-deformed-antidominant-projective]] the translation functor identifies the deformed antidominant projectives along the wall, and the resulting equivalence $V_\mu\theta_s M\cong \operatorname{Res}V_\lambda M$ (restriction of scalars along $C^s\hookrightarrow C$) is upgraded by adjunction to the tensor formula $V\theta_s\cong C\otimes_{C^s}C\otimes_C V$; the graded form is the identification of $C\otimes_{C^s}C$ with the specialization at $S_+$ of the polynomial Soergel bimodule $S\otimes_{S^s}S(1)$, whose right-coinvariant quotient is the reduced module of [[def-reduced-soergel-module-and-dominant-lefschetz-operator]]. The bimodule and shift conventions are those of [[def-type-a-soergel-bimodule-for-a-simple-reflection]] and [[def-the-type-a-soergel-category]], and the generator degrees in the rank-one case are the standard ones.

items.title: Indecomposable projectives correspond to indecomposable Soergel modules
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. The Soergel functor $V$ of [[def-the-antidominant-projective-and-the-soergel-functor]] restricts to an equivalence of categories $$V\colon \operatorname{Proj}(\mathcal O_\lambda)\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\{\text{ungraded direct summands of the }C\otimes_{C^{s}}C\cdots\},\quad P(w\cdot\lambda)\mapsto \bar B_w,$$ between the projective objects of the regular integral block and the category of Soergel modules over the coinvariant algebra obtained from the reduced type-A Soergel bimodules by killing the positive-degree right action; the indecomposable projective $P(w\cdot\lambda)$ corresponds to the indecomposable reduced Soergel module $\bar B_w$ of [[lem-rational-and-real-type-a-soergel-characters-and-indecomposable-labels-agree]], and the correspondence is compatible with the labelings of both sides by $W$ via [[thm-indecomposable-type-a-diagrammatic-soergel-objects-are-indexed-by-permutations-and-shifts]]. Along a reduced expression $w=s_1\cdots s_k$ the identification is by induction from the antidominant projective: $VP(w\cdot\lambda)$ is the unique indecomposable direct summand of $V\theta_{s_1}\cdots\theta_{s_k}M(\lambda)$ determined by [[lem-wall-crossing-compositions-produce-the-projective-with-the-top-standard-label]] and [[thm-wall-crossing-under-the-soergel-functor-is-tensoring-with-the-coinvariant-soergel-bimodule]], and its auxiliary grading is the unique one making the reduced module self-dual, normalized so that the rank-one case is generated in degrees $0$ and $2$. Forgetting the auxiliary grading recovers the ungraded category-$\mathcal O$ projective; no graded lift of category $\mathcal O$ is asserted.
items.strategy: The equivalence is [Soe90, Section 2.5, Theorem 11] together with the classification of the indecomposable Soergel modules: the projective generator $P=\bigoplus_z P(z\cdot\lambda)$ makes $\operatorname{Hom}(P,-)$ an equivalence onto modules over $\operatorname{End}(P)$, and the Struktursatz identifies the target with $\operatorname{End}_C(VP)$ for the image $VP$; the description of $VP(z\cdot\lambda)$ by induction along a reduced expression is the last paragraph of [Soe90, Section 2.5] (as a direct summand of the iterated $C\otimes_{C^{s}}C\otimes\cdots\otimes\mathbb C$). The comparison with the reduced polynomial Soergel bimodules is the compatibly shifted specialization $B_w\mapsto \bar B_w$ of [[def-reduced-soergel-module-and-dominant-lefschetz-operator]], and self-duality fixes the grading up to the stated normalization.

items.title: Verma-flag multiplicities are standard-filtration ranks under V
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice. Let $\mathcal O_\lambda$ be a regular integral block, $P\in\mathcal O_\lambda$ projective with finite Verma flag, and let $C=\operatorname{End}(P(w_0\cdot\lambda))$ and $V$ be as above. Then for every $y\in W$ the Verma-flag multiplicity of $\Delta(y\cdot\lambda)$ in $P$ equals the total graded Bruhat-support rank of $V(P)$ at the label $y$, evaluated at $v=1$: $$(P:\Delta(y\cdot\lambda))=\sum_{d\in\mathbb Z}\big(VP:\Delta_y(d)\big),$$ where the right-hand side counts, in the auxiliary grading of the graded $C$-module $VP$, the total multiplicity of the graded standard object supported at $y$. Equivalently, the ordinary Verma-flag multiplicities of the projective $P$ are obtained from the graded character of $VP$ by forgetting the auxiliary grading; in particular $(P(w\cdot\lambda):\Delta(y\cdot\lambda))$ is the evaluation at $v=1$ of the $y$-supported graded multiplicity in $VP(w\cdot\lambda)$.
items.strategy: The comparison is [Soe90, Section 2.2 and Section 2.6]: the deformation of the projective $P$ over the local ring of $S$ has, by [[prop-base-change-freeness-and-specialization-in-the-deformed-family]], generic specializations with Verma constituents $M(x\cdot\lambda+\epsilon)$ whose multiplicities are the ranks of the graded pieces of the $S$-module $V(P)$ (the supports over $S$ are the weight labels, computed by the weight decomposition of Lemma 1), while [[thm-projectives-in-category-o-have-verma-flags]] and the constancy of finite Verma-flag multiplicities over the family identify these ranks with the Verma multiplicities of the special fiber; the graded bookkeeping is the support filtration of [[def-reduced-soergel-module-and-dominant-lefschetz-operator]] transported across the correspondence of [[thm-indecomposable-projectives-correspond-to-indecomposable-soergel-modules]], evaluated at $v=1$ to forget the auxiliary grading.

title: Projective Functors and the Soergel Functor in Category O — Examples

items.title: The wall-crossing functor on Verma modules in rank one
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice, inherited from the published items used. Work in type $A_1$: $\mathfrak g=\mathfrak{sl}_2(\mathbb C)$, $W=\{1,s\}$, regular integral block, $\Delta_1=M(0)$ and $\Delta_s=M(s\cdot0)=M(-2)$, with the wall the zero weight and $L(\nu)$ the two-dimensional simple for the translating weight. Then $T^\mu_\lambda\Delta(w\cdot\lambda)\cong\Delta(w\cdot\mu)$ for $w=1,s$, while $\theta_s\Delta_1$ and $\theta_s\Delta_s$ both have two-factor Verma flags with factors $\Delta_1,\Delta_s$ each of multiplicity one: $0\to\Delta_1\to\theta_s\Delta_1\to\Delta_s\to0$ and $0\to\Delta_s\to\theta_s\Delta_s\to\Delta_1\to0$ up to the ordering of the factors, and on the Grothendieck group $[\theta_s\Delta_w]=[\Delta_w]+[\Delta_{ws}]$. The example verifies the two-step formula in the smallest case and shows that the length function, not the group order, governs the flag.
items.strategy: Apply [[thm-translation-to-and-from-a-wall-on-standard-modules]] with the translating weight the highest weight of the natural two-dimensional module; the wall is the zero weight of $\mathfrak{sl}_2$ and the stabilizer is $\{1,s\}$. On standard modules the computation is the rank-one instance of [[lem-wall-crossing-functors-act-on-standard-modules-by-the-two-step-extension]]: the two factors are exactly the two standard modules of the block, and the multiplicities are read off from the published statement, which gives each factor with multiplicity one; the Grothendieck-group identity is then immediate from [[def-verma-flag-and-its-multiplicities]]. The rank-one specialization avoids all higher Bruhat combinatorics and can be checked directly inside the block of $\mathfrak{sl}_2$.

items.title: The class map and the wall-crossing action in rank two
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice, inherited from the published items used. In type $A_2$ with simple reflections $s,t$ of order three, the classes of the standards in the regular integral block are $[\Delta_1],[\Delta_s],[\Delta_t],[\Delta_{st}],[\Delta_{ts}],[\Delta_{sts}]$, and the class map sends them to the elements of $W=S_3$; the wall-crossing functors act by right multiplication by $1+s$ and $1+t$, so that $$[\theta_s\theta_t\Delta_1]=[\Delta_1]+[\Delta_t]+[\Delta_s]+[\Delta_{ts}]$$ while $$[\theta_t\theta_s\Delta_1]=[\Delta_1]+[\Delta_s]+[\Delta_t]+[\Delta_{st}],$$ exhibiting the non-commutativity of the wall-crossing action and matching the multiplication of the corresponding standard generators in the Hecke algebra of $S_3$. The example also computes the standard multiplicities of the projective $\theta_s\theta_t\Delta_1$: by the unitriangularity of BGG reciprocity the indecomposable summand $P(st\cdot\lambda)$ occurs with multiplicity one and the remaining summands have smaller labels.
items.strategy: Read off the class formula from [[lem-wall-crossing-functors-act-on-the-grothendieck-group-by-right-multiplication-by-one-plus-s]] applied first to $\Delta_1$ and then to the two-factor objects; the two computations differ in the label of the length-two factor ($ts$ versus $st$), which are distinct elements of $S_3$ and hence distinct Verma classes by the standard basis theorem [[prop-the-grothendieck-group-of-o-has-simple-and-standard-bases]]. The projective multiplicities follow from [[lem-wall-crossing-compositions-produce-the-projective-with-the-top-standard-label]] with the unitriangularity of the Verma-flag matrix.

items.title: The coinvariant algebra of S_2 and S_3 as graded regular representations
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice, inherited from the published items used. For $W=S_2$ acting on $\mathfrak h$ of dimension one: $C=\mathbb k[x]/(x^2)$, of Hilbert series $1+t^2$ in the page normalization $\deg x=2$ (equivalently $1+t$ for $\deg x=1$), with $C_0$ the trivial and $C_2$ the sign representation, so $C$ is the regular representation of $S_2$ with graded multiplicities one and one. For $W=S_3$ acting on the two-dimensional reflection representation: $C=\mathbb k[x_1,x_2,x_3]/(e_1,e_2,e_3)$ has Hilbert series $(1+t^2)(1+t^2+t^4)=1+2t^2+2t^4+t^6$ in the same normalization (equivalently $(1+t)(1+t+t^2)$ for $\deg x_i=1$) and decomposes as $C_0=$ trivial, $C_2=$ standard, $C_4=$ standard$\otimes$sign, $C_6=$ sign, the graded lift of the regular representation with graded multiplicities $1$ for the trivial module, $t^6$ for the sign module and $t^2+t^4$ for the two-dimensional standard module. In both cases the graded character identity of [[thm-the-weyl-coinvariant-algebra-is-the-graded-regular-representation]] evaluates to the regular representation's character and the sum of the graded multiplicities times dimensions recovers $|W|$.
items.strategy: Direct computation of the quotient by the basic invariants in the given coordinates; the Hilbert series is [[lem-weyl-coinvariant-hilbert-series-has-order-w-dimension]] with the basic degrees $1,2$ (respectively $1,2,3$); the identification of the graded pieces with the named $S_n$-modules is by comparing characters at the transpositions and the three-cycle, and the conclusion is the general theorem. The example is a verification of the general statement in the smallest cases and is not used as evidence for it.

items.title: Wall-crossing functors do not commute
items.statement: Assume the Axiom of Choice, inherited from the published items used. In type $A_2$ with distinct simple reflections $s,t$, the projective functors $\theta_s\theta_t$ and $\theta_t\theta_s$ on the regular integral block are not naturally equivalent: on the standard object $\Delta(\lambda)$ their classes are $[\Delta(\lambda)]+[\Delta(t\cdot\lambda)]+[\Delta(s\cdot\lambda)]+[\Delta(ts\cdot\lambda)]$ and $[\Delta(\lambda)]+[\Delta(s\cdot\lambda)]+[\Delta(t\cdot\lambda)]+[\Delta(st\cdot\lambda)]$, which differ because $st\neq ts$ and the Verma classes are linearly independent. So the wall-crossing functors do not define a representation of $W$; they categorify the Hecke algebra of $W$, in which $H_sH_t\neq H_tH_s$ for $m_{st}=3$, rather than the group algebra. The counterexample is the functor-level sharpening of the rank-two class computation and shows that 'generated by wall-crossing' cannot be read as 'representation of $W$'.
items.strategy: Compute both classes with [[lem-wall-crossing-functors-act-on-the-grothendieck-group-by-right-multiplication-by-one-plus-s]], using that the Verma classes are a basis ([[def-verma-flag-and-its-multiplicities]] and the standard-basis theorem for the Grothendieck group); the labels $st$ and $ts$ are distinct elements of $S_3$, and the two induced operators on the standard generators differ, so the induced operators on $K_0$ differ. By the determination theorem [[thm-indecomposable-projective-functors-are-indexed-by-the-weyl-group]](3) a difference on the Grothendieck group implies that the functors are not naturally equivalent; the standard objects generate the Grothendieck group, so it suffices to evaluate on the single object $\Delta(\lambda)$. No claim is made about the existence of a nontrivial natural transformation; the obstruction is already the class.
